dedupe_keys.name: public transportation open data center odpt japan

description: The Public Transportation Open Data Center is Japan's shared platform for open public transport data, run by the Association for Open Data of Public Transportation since 31 May 2019. It publishes static and real-time data from member operators, including the Tokyo Metropolitan Bureau of Transportation, Tokyo Metro, JR East, Keio, Tobu, the Yokohama City Transportation Bureau and many regional bus, tram and ferry operators, together with datasets from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism. Its catalogue listed 362 datasets when read, tagged bus (162), railway (129), bus real-time (37), ferry (30) and demand-responsive transport (15), covering timetables, routes, stations, station timetables, passenger counts and train and bus positions. Coverage is national in principle, with the densest data for the Tokyo region. Formats are the ODPT JSON API, GTFS and GTFS-JP, GTFS Realtime (Protocol Buffers), GTFS-Flex and GBFS; licences vary by dataset between the ODPT basic licence, CC BY, the Public Data License 1.0, CC0 and a licence limited to the annual Open Data Challenge. Use is free but the API needs a free developer registration, and users must follow the terms shown on the developer site. Caveats: terms differ per operator, some data are only open for the challenge period, and not all operators take part. The data support network flow, capacity planning and service resilience studies of Japanese public transport and railways, and pair with the national railway line data (N02) catalogued here.
